title: Rocks and Minerals: The Building Materials of the Crust

questions.question: A naturally occurring, inorganic substance with a definite chemical composition and crystal structure is a:
questions.rationale: That is the definition of a mineral; a rock is an aggregate of one or more minerals, such as granite mixing quartz, feldspar, and mica.

questions.question: Which mineral sits at the top of the Mohs hardness scale?
questions.rationale: Diamond rates 10 on the Mohs scale, quartz 7, and talc only 1.

questions.question: Why does granite show large, visible crystals?
options: It cooled rapidly on the surface
questions.rationale: Granite is an intrusive (plutonic) igneous rock; slow cooling underground lets large crystals grow, unlike rapidly chilled, fine-grained basalt.

questions.question: Basalt is an example of:
questions.rationale: Basalt is extrusive (volcanic) igneous rock formed when lava cools quickly in the open air.

questions.question: Which rock family alone can contain fossils?
questions.rationale: Only sedimentary rocks preserve fossils, because they form from deposited remains and debris layered under low temperatures.

questions.question: Coal is classified as which type of sedimentary rock?
questions.rationale: Coal is an organic sedimentary rock formed from compacted plant remains; chalk is another organic example.

questions.question: Marble is the metamorphic product of:
questions.rationale: Limestone recrystallises into marble; shale becomes slate and sandstone becomes quartzite.

questions.question: Slate forms from the metamorphism of:
questions.rationale: Shale, under heat and pressure, realigns its mica crystals and becomes slate, which splits into roofing sheets.

questions.question: The Deccan Traps of peninsular India erupted about:
questions.rationale: The Deccan Traps flood basalts were erupted roughly 66 million years ago, near the end of the Cretaceous period.

questions.question: In the rock cycle, sedimentary rock buried deep in the crust may next become:
questions.rationale: Heat and pressure metamorphose sedimentary rock; only later, by deep melting, does it return to magma — closing the cycle.
